image_prompt.text: A spiralling chain of ice platforms wrapping the mountain from the wide snowy base up through lower, middle and upper bands to the peak, each platform spaced so a player can jump from one to the next
The ice mountain itself as landform: a broad snowy base rising about 100 studs through frozen cliff walls to a narrow summit, in icy blue, white and cyan with neon accents
Thin ice bridges crossed like tightropes between sections of the spiral, and frozen cliff faces scrambled up where the platforms break off
The lava floor under the mountain — every surface off the ice platforms is lethal on contact, so the ground itself is the thing being survived
A wide safe platform at the very summit, flat and roomy enough for several players to stand on together, ringed with neon-accented ice
Clusters of glowing cyan ice crystal formations growing off the platforms and the frozen cliff walls

layout_placement.text: End-of-climb reward area on the summit platform, where players who reach the top out of the lava collect the payoff

notes: Mix: obby-platformer leads and owns the shape — the prompt is about a spiralling platform climb the player jumps at their own pace — and it brings the genre-wide P6, which is right here because physics-legal platform spacing is the whole map. survival is named because the prompt self-declares a "floor is lava survival game"; its contribution deduped into hazard-kill, presented in Obby's wording as the dominant genre.

survival's terrain-tiered (raised safe spots to climb when the ground burns) was considered and dropped as duplicative — the tower course and path-track already are the raised safe ground above the lava.

Preset kept as Tower Obby with its shape, but obstacle-timing was dropped: the prompt gives an explicit include list and never asks for vanishing or timed platforms, and adding them would build a mechanic the user did not name.

terrain-relief is a Universal Option, used only because the prompt explicitly asks for the ice mountain and frozen cliff walls as landform. Its P0 + tiered elevation is subsumed by the shape's P2, so it is not listed separately.

Route: course-tower is P6 + P2 because platforms in a spiral ascent sit above each other and the thin ice bridges span over lower sections. P2 is not a shape on the override list and the prompt states the stacking, so it stands. Close call against course-terraced (P6 + tiered), which would keep the whole build on the proven pipeline at the cost of the spiral wrapping back over itself; "spiraling upward" decided it.
P2 is not ready to ship yet, so the overhang handling is deferred rather than downgraded silently.

The large snowy base platform is carried in the shape and in path-track / terrain-relief text rather than as social-hub: the prompt asks for a wide starting platform, not a hub with a shop or stage select.
No checkpoint-respawn: the prompt does not mention checkpoints, and this genre's notes say they are near-universal but not universal, so it was left unasked rather than assumed.
"About 100 studs high" and "multiple levels" are kept in text, not as count — the height is a dimension rather than a quantity of a pick, and "multiple" is not a stated number.

would have asked: Sounds like a tower climb — a spiralling ice course from a wide snowy base up about 100 studs to a safe summit platform, with thin ice bridges and frozen cliff walls to scramble, and the lava floor lethal the moment you leave the ice. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself?

would have asked: because platforms spiral back over each other, this needs overhanging surfaces, which is a build step that isn't ready yet — would you accept stepped terraces up the mountain instead, with nothing sitting directly above anything, so it builds on the proven pipeline today?
would have asked: do you want checkpoints on the way up, so a fall into the lava restarts you at the last band rather than at the bottom?
would have asked: should any of the thin ice platforms crack and vanish after you step on them, or should every platform be permanent?
would have asked: anything else you want in the space?
